findings.title: Unsubscribe state change is exposed as a GET request
findings.body: The new GET route invokes `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which immediately modifies the current user's TopicUser notification level. Because GET requests are not protected by Rails CSRF verification and `check_xhr` is explicitly skipped for this action, any third-party page can cause a logged-in visitor's browser to request a known topic's unsubscribe URL (for example via an image or navigation) and silently change that user's notification preference. Render a confirmation page on GET and require a CSRF-protected POST/PUT for the state change, or use a purpose-specific signed token if one-click email unsubscribe is required.

findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil for a logged-in user who has permission to view a topic but has never visited it or otherwise had a topic-user record created. The route is publicly reachable by any logged-in user, not only recipients of the particular email. The subsequent `tu.notification_level` dereference raises `NoMethodError`, returning a 500 instead of allowing the notification preference to be set. Use `TopicUser.change` (which creates missing rows) or explicitly create/fetch the record before reading and saving it.
